letters.title: OCC stablecoin issuer rule (MVEP anchor)
letters.headline: Comment to the OCC on its stablecoin issuer rule, applying the MVEP
letters.h1: Comment to the OCC: applying the Minimum Viable Equivalence Pack to its rule for permitted payment stablecoin issuers
letters.description: Applies the MVEP ten-category diligence framework to the OCC's proposed rule for permitted payment stablecoin issuers. Three recommendations on holder rights, collateral, and equivalence assessment.
letters.agency_long: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
letters.thesis: Three tokenized Treasury products under three regimes receive comparable collateral treatment on Binance through Ceffu, with no disclosure of which instrument backs a given trade.
letters.gaps: Gaps: collateral interoperability is unregulated; money services business capital runs roughly 22-to-1 below the banking-law equivalent for a $40B issuer.

recommendations.ask: Require permitted payment stablecoin issuers to publish a holder-rights analysis
recommendations.text: Require permitted payment stablecoin issuers to publish a holder-rights analysis under applicable commercial law, specifically addressing the defect in the Uniform Commercial Code's qualifying-purchaser rule for digital assets and the owner-vs-controller ambiguity, with compensating measures disclosed (insurance, make-whole commitments, recovery procedures).

recommendations.ask: Coordinate interagency on the collateral eligibility boundary.
recommendations.text: Coordinate interagency on the collateral eligibility boundary. The OCC should coordinate with the SEC, Federal Reserve, FDIC, FinCEN, and Treasury on whether tokenized instruments from different regulatory regimes should receive equivalent collateral treatment without a standardized equivalence assessment.

recommendations.ask: Adopt a standardized equivalence assessment as a supervisory tool.
recommendations.text: Adopt a standardized equivalence assessment as a supervisory tool. MVEP or a comparable framework, producing reproducible assessments that distinguish instruments with different risk profiles. A quarterly or semiannual update cadence reviewed by OCC examiners during regular supervision; estimated cost $5,000 to $15,000 annually per issuer.

supplements.note: Supplements the OCC comment of record (No. 1) with the control-layer frame.

letters.title: OCC Supplemental (control-layer)
letters.headline: OCC stablecoin issuer rule: supplemental comment (control-layer extension)
letters.h1: Supplemental comment to the OCC on its stablecoin issuer rule: control-layer framework extension
letters.description: Supplements the OCC anchor filing on the SEC staff statement on Covered User Interface Providers. Surfaces protection- and supervisory-gradient inversions.
letters.agency_long: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
letters.thesis: A user transacting in a stablecoin from a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, through an interface covered by the SEC staff statement on Covered User Interface Providers, receives none of the twelve interface-conduct conditions; the protection gradient is inverted.
letters.gaps: Gaps: interface-layer asymmetry between crypto-asset-securities and payment-stablecoin transactions on the same interface; no third-party diligence framework attaches.

recommendations.ask: Require permitted payment stablecoin issuers to exercise diligence over distribution interfaces
recommendations.text: Require permitted payment stablecoin issuers to exercise diligence over distribution interfaces under the OCC's existing third-party risk management authority. Calibrated to conduct conditions comparable to the SEC's twelve. No new regulatory authority or interagency coordination required.
components: Mandate three-category disclosure at the point of transaction. (a) Legal claim (statutory entitlement vs contractual right vs trust interest vs bankruptcy priority). (b) Reserve composition (federally insured deposits vs short-term Treasuries vs money market fund shares vs repos). (c) Reserve location and custody (named institutions, jurisdictions, counterparty exposures). Substantive disclosure obligation on the issuer; access obligation on the interface.

Alternative: a joint OCC-SEC interpretation clarifying how the two regimes interact when the same interface facilitates transactions in both crypto asset securities and payment stablecoins. Not mutually exclusive with the primary recommendation.

letters.title: Treasury GENIUS (state-similarity)
letters.headline: Treasury GENIUS Act state-similarity comment
letters.h1: Treasury GENIUS Act state-similarity comment: six recommendations for the substantial-similarity assessment
letters.description: Letter to Treasury on substantial similarity for state GENIUS Act regimes: six recommendations on diagnostics, reserves, capital, scope, insolvency, conduct.
letters.thesis: Treasury must judge fifty state frameworks substantially similar to the federal GENIUS Act framework; the proposed principles reduce this to section-by-section comparison against statutory text.
letters.gaps: Gaps: text-matching cannot detect functional-dimension drift across reserve transparency, capital adequacy, activity scope, insolvency, and interface-layer conduct.

recommendations.ask: Adopt a standardized diagnostic framework
recommendations.text: Adopt a standardized diagnostic framework (MVEP or comparable) for the substantial-similarity assessment, structured around functional holder-protection dimensions rather than statutory sections.

recommendations.ask: Incorporate the three-category reserve disclosure
recommendations.text: Incorporate the three-category reserve disclosure (legal claim, composition, location/custody) as uniform cross-state data fields for Stablecoin Certification Review Committee comparability.

recommendations.ask: Require disclosure of redemption pathway dependencies.
recommendations.text: Require disclosure of redemption pathway dependencies. A regime meeting two-business-day redemption but not disclosing when the sole redemption route depends on another tokenized instrument (as BUIDL depends on USDC) leaves holders exposed.

recommendations.ask: Permit states to narrow but not expand permitted reserve assets.
recommendations.text: Permit states to narrow but not expand permitted reserve assets. Narrowing strengthens holder protection; expanding enables arbitrage.

recommendations.ask: Operational backstop should include custodial diversification.
recommendations.text: Operational backstop should include custodial diversification. The Silicon Valley Bank episode indicates concentration, not operating-capital inadequacy, as the transmission channel.

recommendations.ask: Explicitly recognize interface-layer conduct standards under the principles for additional state requirements
recommendations.text: Explicitly recognize interface-layer conduct standards, under the proposed principles for additional state requirements, as permissible and encouraged additional state requirements, preserved from future federal preemption under the GENIUS Act's carve-out for state consumer protection laws.

letters.title: FDIC: how a bank's subsidiary applies to issue stablecoins
letters.headline: Comment to the FDIC on its application rule for stablecoin-issuing subsidiaries
letters.h1: Comment to the FDIC on its stablecoin application rule: the application as the FDIC's first control-layer topology map
letters.description: FDIC application rule for stablecoin-issuing subsidiaries: first chance to map a prospective issuer's control-layer topology. Four content recommendations plus one anti-money-laundering observation.

comment_period.note: extended from the original February 17, 2026 deadline by a Federal Register notice published February 11, 2026; an extension of about three months

letters.thesis: The application is the FDIC's first chance to map a prospective permitted payment stablecoin issuer's control-layer topology, shaping both the approval decision and the baseline for ongoing supervision.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the contents the proposed rule requires in an application do not surface the structural features (operator, custodian, interface, sweep) that are consequential for either decision.

recommendations.ask: Structured mapping of the activities the GENIUS Act permits an issuer
recommendations.text: Structured mapping of the activities the GENIUS Act permits an issuer, in the application's description of proposed activities: two-axis matrix of (a) the permitted activity categories (issuing, redeeming, managing reserves, custody and safekeeping, supporting activities, and authorized incidental activities) against (b) performing entity (the issuer, its parent bank, an affiliate, a third party, or a combination). Coordinates with parallel topology mapping in the FinCEN and OFAC rulemaking on issuer programs.

recommendations.ask: Preserve the regulator's flexibility to add approval factors.
recommendations.text: Preserve the regulator's flexibility under the GENIUS Act to add approval factors for safety and soundness. Final rule preamble should state that declining to add factors now does not foreclose later additions. Four candidate considerations for future factors: control-layer observability; smart contract immutability; public blockchain dependencies; reserve custody concentration beyond composition.

recommendations.ask: Expand the asset management plan required in the application
recommendations.text: Expand the asset management plan required in the application to include named custodians, per-institution concentration limits as percentage of total reserves, diversification rationale with single-institution failure analysis, and specific treatment of parent-bank-as-custodian concentration.

recommendations.ask: Customer agreements must include a rights-parity assessment
recommendations.text: Customer agreements filed with the application must include a rights-parity assessment: (a) contractual-claim-not-deposit-claim characterization; (b) redemption limit circumstances including qualifying-purchaser scenarios under the Uniform Commercial Code's digital asset rules; (c) disclosure of those rules' asymmetric effects; (d) disclosure of the solvency relationship between the issuer and its parent bank.

letters.title: FinCEN: anti-money-laundering program rule
letters.headline: Comment to FinCEN on its proposed anti-money-laundering program rule
letters.h1: Comment to FinCEN on its anti-money-laundering program rule: anti-money-laundering regulation as structurally a control-layer regime
letters.description: First structural anti-money-laundering reform since the Anti-Money Laundering Act of 2020, covering eleven financial-institution categories. Seven recommendations on control-layer risk.
letters.thesis: Anti-money-laundering regulation has always been control-layer regulation: the Bank Secrecy Act attaches obligations to intermediaries, not to transactions or instruments.
letters.gaps: Gaps: tokenized-finance intermediation disaggregates across issuer, custodian, interface, router, sweep, and hold-and-freeze layers; the proposed risk-based directive does not articulate this compatibility.

recommendations.ask: Clarify that risk assessment processes for tokenized finance must evaluate control-layer exposure.
recommendations.text: Clarify that risk assessment processes for tokenized finance must evaluate control-layer exposure. Business activities should explicitly include the control-layer functions the institution performs.

recommendations.ask: Articulate a disqualifying-activities analog
recommendations.text: Articulate a disqualifying-activities analog for tokenized-finance operators, paralleling the twelve conditions in the SEC staff statement on Covered User Interface Providers.

recommendations.ask: Integrate risks related to permitted payment stablecoin issuers into the anti-money-laundering priorities update
recommendations.text: Integrate risks related to permitted payment stablecoin issuers into the anti-money-laundering priorities update, including the custodial concentration channel and financial-stability considerations.

recommendations.ask: Preserve and clarify the requirement for a US-based anti-money-laundering officer
recommendations.text: Preserve and clarify the requirement for a US-based anti-money-laundering officer for tokenized finance, ensuring effective supervisory control over US-nexus operations.

recommendations.ask: Calibrate independent testing requirements for control-layer verification
recommendations.text: Calibrate independent testing requirements for control-layer verification: on-chain activities, enforcement capability functionality, identity verification coverage across all control-layer functions.

recommendations.ask: Apply the supervision and enforcement consultation framework beyond banks
recommendations.text: Apply the supervision and enforcement consultation framework beyond banks, with priority for large money services businesses operating in tokenized finance.

recommendations.ask: Coordinate the final rule with the FinCEN-OFAC stablecoin issuer rule and the banking agencies' joint anti-money-laundering rule
recommendations.text: Coordinate the final rule with the FinCEN-OFAC stablecoin issuer rule and the banking agencies' joint anti-money-laundering rule, with specific attention to the coordination gap left by the Federal Reserve Board's non-participation.

letters.description: FDIC Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions standards for stablecoin issuers: one reproducible control-posture record for the FDIC and FinCEN to reason over. Six recommendations.
letters.thesis: The FDIC's supervision-and-coordination layer over an issuer's anti-money-laundering and sanctions program works only when the FDIC and FinCEN read the same measured control posture of one operator.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the effective-program disposition is left attestation-shaped; nothing keys the FDIC-to-FinCEN consultation to a shared, reproducible control-posture record.

recommendations.ask: Observable effective-program criteria
recommendations.text: Observable effective-program criteria. Rest the effective-program disposition on observable, reproducible indicators drawn from the FinCEN program requirements, not attestation alone, so a program is not treated as effective merely because policies or attestations exist. Prevents the disposition, which by the rule's terms shields a qualifying issuer from anti-money-laundering enforcement, from becoming a paper-program safe harbor.

recommendations.ask: A shared control-posture record
recommendations.text: A shared control-posture record. Make a reproducible control-posture record a standing component of the FDIC-to-FinCEN notice package, so both agencies reason over the same measured object rather than reconstructing two records inside the notice window.

recommendations.ask: Thresholds keyed to posture
recommendations.text: Thresholds keyed to posture. Pair any outstanding-issuance-value threshold or issuer-requested consultation option with a control-posture trigger keyed to the same record, and account for a suspension or revocation under the GENIUS Act's enforcement provision premised in part on anti-money-laundering deficiencies.
recommendations.refs: Questions 2 and 3; Sections 350.200 and 350.202; GENIUS Act section 6(b)

recommendations.ask: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability
recommendations.text: Operational test of block, freeze, and reject capability. Require examination evidence that the sanctions capability works across both primary and secondary channels, with examination intensity scaled to measured holder concentration, rather than inferring it from the parent program or from the presence of on-chain functions.

recommendations.ask: An accountable line for parent-program reliance
recommendations.text: An accountable line for parent-program reliance. Where an issuer leverages its parent institution's program, confirm that one identifiable accountable line holds both the issuer-specific control-posture information and the authority to act on it, so delegation does not diffuse responsibility.

recommendations.ask: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes
recommendations.text: Coverage across holding-location obligor changes. Where a single tokenized instrument changes its obligor and applicable regime based on holding location, confirm that anti-money-laundering and sanctions coverage follows the instrument across the transition, treating the boundary crossing as a monitored event with continuity of identity and lawful-order controls.

letters.description: SEC Draft Strategic Plan for fiscal years 2026 to 2030: the plan's digital-asset objectives turn on a measurement capability it does not yet name.
letters.thesis: Where the plan's digital-asset objectives turn on whether a system is decentralized, decentralization must be measured against a reproducible standard the plan does not yet name.
letters.gaps: Gaps: naive holder lists inflate measured concentration 2.3x median (up to ~18x); launch allocation does not predict where control settles (r = 0.09).

recommendations.ask: Name reproducible measurement as the foundation capability
recommendations.text: Name reproducible measurement as the foundation capability. Name independent, reproducible measurement of digital-asset concentration and control as the capability the regulatory foundation rests on, so that any threshold the Commission later adopts rests on a method an outside party can reproduce from public on-chain data.

recommendations.ask: Frame oversight at the operator level, not the token level alone
recommendations.text: Frame oversight at the operator level, not the token level alone (custody, trading, and staking). Structural risk frequently concentrates at the operator rather than the token: the operator scoring highest on regulatory intensity experienced a 10 to 13 percent depeg during the March 2023 stress while a lower-scoring operator held its peg, and a single transfer agent serves all three documented tokenization strategies. Assess an operator across its full portfolio alongside token-level classification.

recommendations.ask: Measure decentralization wherever a boundary or jurisdictional determination turns on it
recommendations.text: Measure decentralization wherever a boundary or jurisdictional determination turns on it (boundaries of securities law and jurisdiction). Where the securities-law boundary or the SEC-CFTC allocation rests on the degree of a system's decentralization, measure that degree from current on-chain state, supported by indicators of current concentration and realized voting control, rather than inferring it from holder counts or disclosed allocations.

recommendations.ask: Build reproducible on-chain instruments into advanced analytics
recommendations.text: Build reproducible on-chain instruments into advanced analytics. Two dollar stablecoins on the same chain carried top-100 holder concentrations roughly five times apart in a single snapshot; reproducible concentration and control instruments, developed on public data, are adaptable to the registered products the Commission reviews. The offer is method transfer, not findings about registered products.

recommendations.ask: Codify the account-definition boundary
recommendations.text: Codify the account-definition boundary. Move the preamble footnote's disclaimer into regulatory text, so the customer identification definition of account cannot be read into the lawful-order obligation that the proposed customer identification section preserves. Carries forward the position already on the record in the FinCEN-OFAC stablecoin issuer rulemaking (wallet address as account for lawful orders) by citation rather than re-argument. recommendations.text: Observable hallmarks of a formal relationship. Retain "formal relationship" but state its hallmarks as observable attributes, stated non-exclusively: a contractual right of redemption against the issuer, an onboarding record, membership on an authorized-participant or minter list, a custody agreement. Reconcile with the "contractual or other business relationship" formulation in the mutual fund customer identification program rule, which one of the proposal's own footnotes flags. A relationship test that turns on the issuer's characterization of it is not examinable.

recommendations.ask: Conform the preamble to the codified account text
recommendations.text: Conform the preamble to the codified account text. The preamble describes the account definition's digital asset service provider item with three qualifiers; the codified text reads bare, "Providing services of a digital asset service provider." Resolve in favor of the codified text and correct the preamble: the qualified reading would relieve an issuer of customer identification duties precisely where its activities were unauthorized.

recommendations.text: Reliance asymmetry, and the threshold that determines which side an issuer sits on. letters.description: FDIC resolution submissions: keep the run-risk content the rule would delete; extend the receivership perimeter to tokenized deposits. Six recommendations.
letters.thesis: The rule narrows what covered institutions must submit for resolution planning, and the content it removes is disproportionately the content that predicts a run.
letters.gaps: Gaps: uninsured-deposit concentration and key-depositor detail, the variables March 2023 showed to be decisive, would be deleted while coverage is keyed to asset size alone; the receivership perimeter does not identify tokenized-deposit or stablecoin-reserve-custody arrangements or the operational controls at that boundary.
letters.card_meta: 2026-08-24 · FDIC · Run-risk measurement + control layer · 6 recs

recommendations.ask: A measured run-risk trigger, not size alone
recommendations.text: A measured run-risk trigger, not size alone. Do not de-scope the $50 billion to $100 billion cohort by asset size alone; key continued minimal coverage to a measured uninsured-deposit-concentration or rapid-growth trigger.

recommendations.ask: A retained uninsured-deposit-concentration element
recommendations.text: A retained uninsured-deposit-concentration element. Retain a minimal uninsured-deposit-concentration and key-depositor data element rather than deleting it outright, at a fraction of the burden of the full submission.

recommendations.ask: Tokenized-deposit and reserve-custody linkages in the perimeter
recommendations.text: Tokenized-deposit and reserve-custody linkages in the perimeter (digital-services content). Require identification of tokenized-deposit and stablecoin-reserve-custody arrangements and the operational controls at the boundary, so a receiver knows what it can reach.

recommendations.ask: Current demonstration, not opt-in participation
recommendations.text: Current demonstration, not opt-in participation. Key any reliance on the Resolution Readiness Adjustment to a demonstration that is still current, reconciling the assessments rule's credit with this rule's evidence.

recommendations.ask: A minimal public accountability signal
recommendations.text: A minimal public accountability signal. Retain a minimal, calibrated public section or an equivalent accountability mechanism rather than removing public visibility entirely.

recommendations.ask: One operational-capability test, administered once
recommendations.text: One operational-capability test, administered once. Retain an operational-capability test that the covered institution can deliver the required output under test conditions, reusable as the assessments rule's Resolution Readiness Adjustment test rather than duplicated.

letters.title: FDIC: deposit insurance assessments
letters.headline: FDIC deposit insurance assessments comment
letters.h1: FDIC deposit insurance assessments comment: price the run risk the assessment framework is about to stop pricing
letters.description: FDIC deposit insurance assessments: price the run risk and novel-activity risk the framework is about to stop pricing. Four recommendations.
letters.thesis: The cohort the assessment rule reclassifies carries measurably higher run risk than the cohort it is priced against; the framework prices size and resolvability, not novel-activity exposure.
letters.gaps: Gaps: reclassified banks show higher uninsured and insured brokered deposit shares than the comparison cohort; no indicator reaches crypto-asset or stablecoin-reserve-custody exposure; a voluntary rate-incentivized readiness mechanism selects for the banks least likely to fail, so its loss-reduction rationale is weakest in the non-electing tail.

recommendations.ask: A run-risk factor for the reclassified cohort
recommendations.text: A run-risk factor for the reclassified cohort (the $10 billion to $30 billion threshold). Retain a run-risk-sensitive factor for reclassified banks, or condition the reclassification on a measured uninsured-deposit-concentration or rapid-growth trigger.

recommendations.ask: A novel-activity and concentration risk indicator
recommendations.text: A novel-activity and concentration risk indicator. Add, or solicit comment on adding, a novel-activity and concentration risk indicator to the assessment framework, so the pricing reaches the exposure channel March 2023 demonstrated.

recommendations.ask: A Resolution Readiness Adjustment keyed to a current demonstration
recommendations.text: A Resolution Readiness Adjustment keyed to a current demonstration. Preserve the operational test the proposed text already defines, state the sufficiency standard, reconcile the seven-year data-access reengagement interval with the three-year retest, calibrate the adjustment jointly with the FDIC's companion resolution submissions proposal, and support observable partial credit.

recommendations.ask: Reserve-ratio slippage and the distribution of relief
recommendations.text: Reserve-ratio slippage and the distribution of relief (material economic effects). Weigh the reductions' effect on the fund's recovery and their distribution against the fairness rationale, and state the reasoning: the roughly $4.0 billion per year reduction delays the fund reaching its 2 percent designated reserve ratio to 2035.

letters.title: Federal Reserve: anti-money-laundering programs for the banks it supervises
letters.headline: Comment to the Federal Reserve on its anti-money-laundering program rule
letters.h1: Comment to the Federal Reserve on its anti-money-laundering program rule: adopt the coordination provisions the sibling rules carry, and give content to the term the protection turns on
letters.description: Federal Reserve anti-money-laundering program rule: adopt the FinCEN coordination provisions the sibling rules carry; define the term the protection turns on. Nine recommendations.
letters.agency_long: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
letters.thesis: Four agencies are writing one anti-money-laundering program rule four times, and the only substantive divergence in the Board's version is the coordination mechanism itself.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the Board's proposed rule omits the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions the OCC, FDIC, and NCUA proposals carry, while the Board's Alternatives Considered section states that the proposal includes them.

recommendations.ask: Adopt the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions
recommendations.text: Adopt the two FinCEN consultation and information-sharing provisions (new paragraphs in the Board's proposed rule). The signature contribution. All three sibling rules, proposed by the OCC, the FDIC and the NCUA, contain them. This is the only substantive divergence between this rule and its siblings, and it is the coordination mechanism itself.
recommendations.refs: Question 23; Section 208.63; proposed 12 CFR 21.21(h) and (i), 326.8(h) and (i), and 748.2(h) and (i)

recommendations.ask: State the weighing factors for a significant or systemic failure, and retain the breadth of what the protection covers
recommendations.text: State the weighing factors for a significant or systemic failure, and retain the breadth of what the protection covers. The second signature contribution, and deliberately two-directional. On the trigger: state the factors that bear on the judgment rather than a bright line, which would create the cliff effects the Board itself rejects in its Alternatives Considered section, drawing on the notice's own examples in its discussion of implementing a program, and answer the notice's program-level versus component-level question because it governs the same trigger. The control-layer factor this program adds: a failure at a shared third-party dependency can be systemic in effect while presenting at any single institution as isolated. On the other half, the recommendation is contrarian and asks the Board to change nothing. The definition of a significant anti-money-laundering or counter-terrorist-financing supervisory action describes what the institution is protected from, so narrowing it shrinks the shield; striking unsafe or unsound practices or conditions from it would let an action be recharacterized as a safety-and-soundness matter and escape the rule's enforcement and supervision policy entirely. Breadth there is already bounded by the definition's conjunctive third element and its express examiner-observation carve-out. The American Bankers Association asked the sibling agencies for the same clarification of the trigger a month before this proposal published, and observed that uncertainty about eligibility means the protection will not benefit banks.
recommendations.refs: Questions 6, 7, 21, 22, 24 and 26, and Question 5; Sections 208.63(a) and (g); notice section IV.C.2; Section 208.63(g)

recommendations.ask: Answer the harmonious-function question by enumeration, not intent
recommendations.text: Answer the harmonious-function question by enumeration, not intent. Enumerate each divergence between the Board's final rule and the FinCEN and Agencies final rules, and state the reconciliation for each, rather than stating an intention to align. The second half of the question is answered from the statutory derivation in the notice's own footnote, which contrasts the Bank Secrecy Act's program provision, where a program shall be established, with the Federal Deposit Insurance Act's compliance provision, where it is established and maintained.

recommendations.ask: Key the effective date to the last of the four final rules
recommendations.text: Key the effective date to the last of the four final rules. Key it to the last of the four to issue, or state the interim compliance expectation, because an institution cannot sequence one program against four rules with independent effective dates. On the notice's size-tailoring question the letter declines formal size tailoring, agreeing with the Board's cliff-effect reasoning, while noting that a commensurate-with standard should scale to the risk presented rather than to asset size.

recommendations.ask: Reconcile the operative scope with the regulatory flexibility analysis, and state one small-entity figure
recommendations.text: Reconcile the operative scope with the regulatory flexibility analysis, and state one small-entity figure (regulatory flexibility analysis). Two drafting paths are offered: a defined term in the rule's definitions paragraph, or amending the Board's parallel rules for Edge and agreement corporations and U.S. offices of foreign banks in the same final rule. Separately, the analysis states the small-entity population two ways, approximately 439 in one place and 464 in both cost computations. The arithmetic reconciles only with 464: 32 hours times 51.20 dollars times 464 entities is 760,217.6, printed as 760,218, and 8 times 51.20 times 464 is 190,054.4, printed as 190,054; at 439 entities the same arithmetic yields 719,257.6 and 179,814.4. The letter takes no position on which figure is correct and does not assert the estimate is materially wrong. It asks the final rule to state one number and use it in both places, which is responsive to the notice's own request that commenters describe the number of small entities affected.

recommendations.ask: Confirm that the rule's own distribution-channels definition reaches programmatic and control-layer arrangements
recommendations.text: Confirm that the rule's own distribution-channels definition reaches programmatic and control-layer arrangements. Confirm, rather than add a category: the Board already defines distribution channels as the methods and tools through which a bank opens accounts and provides products or services, including remote and other non-face-to-face means, and already names blockchain monitoring and analytics among encouraged innovative approaches. Confirm that the definition reaches tokenized and programmatic channels and third-party control-layer arrangements, and that a change in those arrangements can require a prompt risk-assessment update. On the notice's alternatives for when a risk assessment must be updated, retain promptly over a set schedule and significantly over materially, the latter because it would import a securities and accounting term of art. On the notice's question about re-approving the written program, the same control-layer change that triggers a prompt update is the natural re-approval trigger, so the two questions should share one test rather than each carrying its own. The letter answers the objection that distribution channels is undefined and will evolve directly: the term is undefined in the codified text and defined only in the preamble, which is exactly why confirming it is the ask, and the evolution concern cuts toward under-inclusion rather than rigidity.
recommendations.refs: Questions 10, 11, 15 and 20; Sections 208.63(c)(1)(i)(A) and (C), and (e); Questions 15 and 20(b)

recommendations.ask: Anchor independent testing and the effectiveness determination in observable criteria
recommendations.text: Anchor independent testing and the effectiveness determination in observable criteria. Carry the notice's own objective-criteria language into the determination, along with its own statement that a program meeting the technical requirements on their face is not what the rule intends. On the notice's resource-allocation question, frame the measure as coverage of identified risk rather than as input volume.

recommendations.ask: Treat banking a permitted payment stablecoin issuer as a distinct channel
recommendations.text: Treat banking a permitted payment stablecoin issuer as a distinct channel. Confirm that a bank holding reserves for, or banking, a permitted payment stablecoin issuer evaluates that relationship as a distinct distribution channel, because the illicit-finance activity occurs among holders who are not the bank's customers and whose transactions never pass through the bank's systems.

recommendations.ask: Make the required accessibility run to authority and information, not location
recommendations.text: Make the required accessibility run to authority and information, not location. Clarify that the accessibility the rule requires of the designated officer runs to that officer's authority and access to information, not to physical location alone, where anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing functions or control-layer operations sit offshore. This has particular force for the covered United States offices of foreign banks, which interacts with the scope recommendation above.

letters.title: CFTC: clearing organization requirements
letters.headline: CFTC clearing organization requirements comment
letters.h1: CFTC clearing organization requirements comment: define the evidentiary form of the tokenized-collateral equivalence determination
letters.description: CFTC clearing organization requirements: define the evidentiary form of the tokenized-collateral equivalence determination clearing organizations must show. Four recommendations.
letters.thesis: Clearing organizations must now show, instrument by instrument, that a tokenized asset conveys the traditional asset's rights, yet the Commission's collection captures that determination in no defined form.
letters.gaps: Gaps: a supervisor can see that a haircut was applied but not whether the instrument conveys the rights the haircut assumes; liquidation-path and redemption-path concentration analysis goes unrecorded; the determination carries no revisit date while haircuts are re-evaluated monthly.

recommendations.ask: Define the evidentiary form of the equivalence determination
recommendations.text: Define the evidentiary form of the equivalence determination. A defined record would capture the decision date, an instrument description sufficient to identify the tokenized collateral and its redemption or liquidation pathway, the framework applied, the outcome for each category, and the system-of-record reference. The five areas of regulatory concern named in the CFTC staff's own letter on tokenized collateral would serve as a first set of categories, so the form needs no framework beyond what Commission staff have already published; the program's MVEP is offered as one more detailed model.

recommendations.ask: Record the liquidation-path analysis behind the liquidity finding the CFTC's margin rule requires.
recommendations.text: Record the liquidation-path analysis behind the liquidity finding the CFTC's margin rule requires. Tokenized collateral posts instantly and converts to cash through redemption paths that can constrict together. The record would capture the paths relied on, the stresses considered, and whether at least one path survives each, which is the analysis the regulation's stressed-conditions language and the unimpeded-liquidation requirement of the CFTC's legal risk rule already call for.

recommendations.ask: Record whether concentration was assessed at the redemption path, not only at the asset
recommendations.text: Record whether concentration was assessed at the redemption path, not only at the asset. A single categorical field. Concentration can sit beneath the asset, in the infrastructure through which it is redeemed: a National Bureau of Economic Research study found that the largest stablecoin issuer allowed six agents in an average month to redeem for cash, against 521 at a second large stablecoin, a difference no asset-level measure reveals.

recommendations.ask: Record when the equivalence determination was last revisited
recommendations.text: Record when the equivalence determination was last revisited. A date and an event class. Haircuts and concentration limits are already re-evaluated at least monthly under the CFTC's margin rule; the determination they rest on has no comparable record, and the date makes staleness visible without the Commission having to set a review interval.

letters.title: FDIC: disclosure of information
letters.headline: FDIC disclosure of information comment
letters.h1: FDIC disclosure of information comment: build the aggregated-analysis channel into the rule, with safeguards
letters.description: FDIC disclosure of information: a standing, safeguarded channel for aggregated analysis of supervisory data, open to researchers. Four recommendations.

comment_period.note: as extended by an FDIC notice published August 28, 2026

letters.thesis: Supervisory material reaches the public by exception; a standing, safeguarded channel for aggregated analysis would let the supervisory process be examined before a failure, not after.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the channel appears only in the preamble, with no regulatory text, purpose, or safeguards; eligibility runs only to law firms and trade associations; a minimum count alone does not protect the largest institutions.

recommendations.ask: Codify the channel and open it to independent researchers
recommendations.text: Codify the channel and open it to independent researchers. Adopt it as a new paragraph of the proposed provision on disclosure by insured depository institutions and other entities that states its purpose, eligibility, and safeguards, and make independent research organizations eligible alongside the law firms and trade associations the preamble names. The OCC's parallel proposal, whose comment period closed the same day, already gives a not-for-profit university or think-tank as an example recipient; consistent criteria across the agencies would let one research design operate under each agency's rule.

recommendations.ask: Keep institution-level data inside a controlled environment
recommendations.text: Keep institution-level data inside a controlled environment. Release only aggregate outputs that pass review. In the simplest form, FDIC staff run approved analyses and release the results, the arrangement the statistical disclosure control literature calls remote execution. No recipient then receives another institution's data, which answers the re-identification risk and the competitor-information concern by design.

recommendations.ask: Protect the largest institutions, not only small cells
recommendations.text: Protect the largest institutions, not only small cells. Require every released statistic to rest on a minimum number of institutions, limit the share any single institution may account for, and review combinations of releases. These are the threshold, dominance, and complementary-suppression rules the federal statistical system already applies to business data.

recommendations.ask: Require reproducible public disclosures
recommendations.text: Require reproducible public disclosures. Any public disclosure based on the channel should state its method and parameters in enough detail for the FDIC to recompute it, and correct any figure the FDIC cannot reproduce. This checks computation, not conclusions, and does not reintroduce the preapproval the proposal removes.

letters.title: Treasury GENIUS (issuance, offer and sale)
letters.headline: Treasury GENIUS Act issuance, offer and sale comment
letters.h1: Treasury GENIUS Act issuance, offer and sale comment: confirm on-chain that a foreign issuer's lawful-order capability exists, then reach the controls around it
letters.description: Letter to Treasury on its GENIUS Act rule for issuing, offering and selling payment stablecoins: an on-chain check that a foreign issuer's lawful-order capability exists, and the controls around it. Seven recommendations.
letters.thesis: Of the two facts a provider's reliance on a foreign issuer's representation turns on under the proposed rule, the issuer's technological capability to comply with a lawful order is readable from its deployed contract and on-chain history, while whether it will comply is not observable at all; the rule should name the observable check as a floor.
letters.gaps: Gaps: a capability check alone would clear an issuer whose controls around the capability are absent; the forward-looking limb has no stated evidence; the mandatory check against the GENIUS Act's noncompliant-issuer designations misses the 30 days between a published determination and the trading prohibition; the authority to invoke the capability can sit with a party other than the signer.

recommendations.ask: On-chain capability check as a diligence floor
recommendations.text: On-chain capability check as a diligence floor. State, in the rule text or the adopting release, that reasonable due diligence on a foreign issuer's representation includes confirming from the deployed contract and its on-chain history that the represented capability to comply with a lawful order exists and that the authority to invoke it is identifiable, where the payment stablecoin is issued on a public ledger. A freeze or burn function either exists in the deployed code or it does not, and prior invocations are a matter of public record, so the check needs no cooperation from the issuer: an examination of the ledger, not an audit.

recommendations.ask: Diligence must reach the controls, not just the capability
recommendations.text: Diligence must reach the controls, not just the capability. Extend the expected diligence to who may invoke the function and under what internal authorization, whether limits exist on the privileged operations the same key can perform, and whether the issuer publishes a response commitment for a lawful order. A documented production overmint at a highly regulated issuer, whose freeze and mint capability scored high on the program's own index while a supply cap, a per-transaction limit and multisignature minting were absent, shows that a check of the capability alone would have cleared it; the comment states this as a limitation of the program's own instrument. The Act already pairs the capability with policies and procedures for permitted issuers.

recommendations.ask: Replace the unobservable "will comply" with an observable proxy
recommendations.text: Replace the unobservable "will comply" with an observable proxy. Confirm that the forward-looking limb is satisfied by the issuer's documented history of responding to lawful orders and a published response commitment, plus a duty to re-check on defined triggers (a change in control arrangements or in the contract's privileged functions, a designation of an affiliated issuer as noncompliant under the GENIUS Act, or a failure to respond to a known lawful order), with records retained; and retain the proposed "knows, has reason to know, or should know" standard over the no-reason-to-suspect alternative.
recommendations.refs: proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) and section 3(b)(2); Questions 52 and 53

recommendations.ask: Key the mandatory check for noncompliant foreign issuers to a published determination
recommendations.text: Key the mandatory check for noncompliant foreign issuers to a published determination. Under the GENIUS Act the trading prohibition takes effect 30 days after its Federal Register notification, so a check limited to a prohibition in effect can pass while the published record already shows noncompliance. Confirm that the mandatory element covers a published determination of noncompliance not since lifted, and state the designation list's current state, where a provider checks it, and whether Treasury will maintain a machine-readable source.
recommendations.refs: proposed Sec. 1523.3(c); section 8, 12 U.S.C. 5907; Question 52; section 8(b)

recommendations.ask: Retain reasonable belief, and name the observable evidence for it
recommendations.text: Retain reasonable belief, and name the observable evidence for it. Keep the reasonable-belief approach over the per se alternatives for both issuance and offers or sales, and name the categories of evidence that support it: deployed geographic-blocking controls and their coverage, sanctions and jurisdictional screening at onboarding, controls against location spoofing, and the handling of indeterminate results. The controls that establish location are themselves observable, so the standard loses nothing on verifiability.
recommendations.refs: proposed Sec. 1523.2(c) and Sec. 1523.3(e); Questions 38, 44, 62 and 64

recommendations.ask: Assess the capability where the invoking authority resides
recommendations.text: Assess the capability where the invoking authority resides. Confirm that the inquiry reaches the party that actually holds the authority to invoke the compliance function, including an affiliate, a foundation, a contract administrator or a multi-party arrangement, because a representation signed by an issuer whose key is held elsewhere describes a capability the signer does not control. No new obligation arises in the ordinary case in which the issuer holds its own keys.
recommendations.refs: proposed Sec. 1523.3(c) and Sec. 1523.1; Question 52, see also Question 24

recommendations.ask: Align the lawful-order test across the three rulemakings that carry it
recommendations.text: Align the lawful-order test across the three rulemakings that carry it. State in the final rule's preamble how this capability standard relates to the lawful-order obligations in the FinCEN permitted payment stablecoin issuer rulemakings: whether an issuer that satisfies one satisfies the others, and whether a provider may rely on a determination made under them. Align the definition of lawful order with FinCEN's, or state where and why the two differ.

letters.title: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets (second SEC comment)
letters.headline: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets comment
letters.h1: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets comment: an observable control condition for the investment contract safe harbor, not the issuer's representations alone
letters.description: SEC Regulation Crypto Assets: test the investment contract safe harbor against control read from on-chain state, not the issuer's word alone. Eight recommendations.
letters.thesis: The proposed investment contract safe harbor conditions a permanent change in a crypto asset's status on facts measurable from public data but tests them only through the issuer's own certification; the more objective standard the SEC asks about has at its core a definition of control the Commission has already written.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the safe harbor tests cessation only through the issuer's own certification about its own promises; it reaches only the issuer, not the affiliates and agents the 2026 Interpretation includes; its scope shrinks with what the issuer promised; it is one-way on its face; and no measurement methodology is specified for holder or voting data.

recommendations.ask: Add an observable control condition to the safe harbor's cessation test
recommendations.text: Add an observable control condition to the safe harbor's cessation test. Both operative facts in that test as proposed are internal to the issuer: whether it has ceased the essential managerial efforts it represented or promised, and whether it intends to make new promises. Add a third condition, satisfied where neither the issuer nor any person acting for it holds a power to alter the associated crypto network or the subject crypto asset that can be exercised without holder approval and takes effect without a timelock during which holders may reject it. That is a yes-or-no fact the issuer already knows and a reviewer can check from the chain. The condition imports no market conception of decentralization: it tests one element of the Commission's own definition of a decentralized crypto system, operational control, in its narrowest, unilateral form.

recommendations.ask: Require the transition report's analysis (Form TR) and specify its minimum content
recommendations.text: Require the transition report's analysis (Form TR) and specify its minimum content. Do not permit certification without analysis, since a certification with no reasoning attached cannot meet the Commission's stated purpose that "a reasonable investor could understand how the issuer made its determination." Specify three minimum elements: a privileged-function inventory of the admin keys, upgrade authorities, mint and freeze functions and equivalent capabilities, with the on-chain address or program identifier at which each resides and who controls each; where the issuer relies on governance dispersion, a governance-participation measurement with the methodology stated, including the address exclusions applied and whether delegated voting power was measured; and a related-person continuation statement on whether any related person is engaged in, or has undertaken to engage in, the efforts the issuer has ceased. Commissioner Peirce's 2021 Token Safe Harbor Proposal 2.0 asked more of its end-of-period exit report than the proposed safe harbor asks of Form TR.
recommendations.refs: proposed Rule 400(b) and Form TR; Questions 128 and 130

recommendations.ask: Extend the cessation condition to affiliates, agents and privileged-function holders
recommendations.text: Extend the cessation condition to affiliates, agents and privileged-function holders. The proposed safe harbor addresses only "the issuer," so an issuer may cease its essential managerial efforts while a founder-controlled foundation, an affiliate or a development company under common control continues them, and the crypto asset still exits the definition of "security" permanently. The 2026 Interpretation that the safe harbor is intended to codify already reads "issuer" to include affiliates and agents of the issuer or a promoter. Extend the condition to those persons and to any other person who controls a privileged function in the Form TR inventory, but not to every related person as the proposal defines the term: not to a consultant, a family member, a validator or a code publisher who is neither an affiliate nor an agent and controls no privileged function. The release's existing carve-out for post-functionality maintenance, which applies "whether by the issuer or another party," keeps ordinary maintenance outside the condition.
recommendations.refs: proposed Rule 400(a); Questions 125 and 127; proposed Rule 100

recommendations.ask: Specify the measurement methodology wherever holder or voting data is relied on
recommendations.text: Specify the measurement methodology wherever holder or voting data is relied on. The same crypto asset can be characterized as dispersed or concentrated depending on choices no rule currently constrains. In the program's fifty-two-protocol audit, excluding burn addresses and protocol-controlled addresses lowered measured concentration by a median factor of 2.3 times across the thirty-two protocols with complete logging, while delegation raised effective voting concentration above post-exclusion holdings in thirteen of eighteen protocols with sufficient governance data (2.5 to 25.6 times, median 4.4 times), with five exceptions where a mature delegate program dispersed voting below holdings. Independent work by Matthias Nadler and Fabian Schär reaches the same conclusion about holder data. Specify, in the rule text or the adopting release, that any holder-concentration measure excludes burn and protocol-controlled addresses and, where governance runs through delegation, reflects delegated voting power rather than token holdings alone. The comment offers the audit's documented corrected methodology and its executable replication package as one reproducible procedure.

recommendations.ask: Anchor the cessation standard to network functionality
recommendations.text: Anchor the cessation standard to network functionality. The cessation standard is scoped by the issuer's own representations, so an issuer that described an extensive development program must complete or abandon all of it, while one that described little has little to cease; that asymmetry runs against the disclosure rule's aim of fuller disclosure. Incorporate the functionality anchor the release already articulates as an independent element, so the condition turns on the state of the network as well as on the completion of what was promised, and define it in the Commission's terms rather than the issuer's, after the 2026 Interpretation's definition of a "functional" crypto system: one whose native crypto asset can be used on the system in accordance with its programmatic utility.
recommendations.refs: proposed Rule 400(a); Questions 131, 132 and 133; proposed Rule 103

recommendations.ask: Condition continued reliance on non-resumption, with prompt notice if efforts resume
recommendations.text: Condition continued reliance on non-resumption, with prompt notice if efforts resume. The safe harbor operates once, and its only forward-looking element is the statement that the issuer "does not intend to make" new representations or promises, which neither the Commission nor investors can observe. Condition continued reliance on the safe harbor on the issuer not resuming essential managerial efforts, and require prompt notice if it does, on the model of the current reports the proposal requires of issuers under ongoing reporting (the suggested rule text gives four business days). On the SEC's question about whether relying on the safe harbor is a tacit admission, state that filing Form TR is not, by itself, an admission that the asset was subject to an investment contract; the filing remains subject to the antifraud provisions. The comment leaves open whether issuers will rely on the 2026 Interpretation instead of the safe harbor, on which it has no evidence.
recommendations.refs: proposed Rule 400, new paragraph (c); Questions 127 and 134

recommendations.ask: State the progress the disclosure rule requires against the milestones the issuer disclosed
recommendations.text: State the progress the disclosure rule requires against the milestones the issuer disclosed. Progress is measurable only against a stated baseline: if the initial disclosure describes undertakings in narrative terms without identifiable milestones, the Form TR completion analysis inherits the same indeterminacy. Require the issuer to identify the specific milestones or deliverables comprising its represented essential managerial efforts and to state progress against each. This is the one place the comment supports a prescriptive element, because the safe harbor later depends on it; otherwise it supports the disclosure rule's principles-based approach. The 2026 Interpretation already treats a business plan containing detailed milestones as the kind of representation that speaks directly to essential managerial efforts.

recommendations.ask: Align the control test with sibling agencies' effective-control standards
recommendations.text: Align the control test with sibling agencies' effective-control standards. State in the adopting release that the safe harbor's cessation determination looks to effective control rather than nominal arrangement, and that placing an effort with an affiliate or agent does not by itself establish cessation, the same diagnostic the program applied in its comments on FinCEN's anti-money-laundering program rule (Recommendation 4) and on the FDIC's Bank Secrecy Act and sanctions standards (Recommendation 5). Divergent tests for who controls a network invite forum selection rather than compliance, and the safe harbor line is becoming a boundary between two regimes: the CFTC's October 5, 2026 advance notice presents its framework as complementary to the safe harbor, so the Form TR record should rest on effective-control facts both agencies can read.
recommendations.refs: adopting release; Questions 127 and 131; FINCEN-2026-0034; RIN 3064-AG29

supplements.note: Corrects two statements about the program's index in Recommendations 1 and 2 of the October 13 comment (No. 22); changes none of the seven recommendations.
