letters.title: SEC: temporary exemptions for trading tokenized stock
letters.headline: SEC tokenized stock exemptions comment
letters.h1: SEC tokenized stock exemptions comment: collect from day one the facts tokenized stock rulemaking will need, in a form checkable against the public ledger
letters.description: Letter to the SEC on its tokenized stock exemptions: collect the ledger facts rulemaking will need, in checkable form. Seven recommendations.

comment_period.note: open-ended request for comment; the Order sets no deadline

letters.thesis: Several of the Order's conditions turn on facts the public ledger already shows, but the Order collects them as descriptions of procedure, only for a venue's own contracts, or not at all; a five-year exemption meant to inform rulemaking should collect them from its first day, in a form checkable against the ledger.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the change-control disclosure reaches only the venue's own contracts, not the tokens in its pools; the same-rights test does not reach the holder's exposure to a failed third-party tokenizer; dollar prices omit the stablecoin conversion rate and the ledger transaction identifier; the public notice's item on clearing and settlement names no legal point of finality for either leg of a trade.

recommendations.ask: Verify equivalence through the custody chain and the holder's position if the tokenizer fails
recommendations.text: Verify equivalence through the custody chain and the holder's position if the tokenizer fails. State that the same-rights verification the Order requires of a venue, and the venue's public-notice description of it, must address five things: the tokenization model; which record controls if the ledger and the off-chain record disagree, and how often token supply is reconciled to the shares held for holders; the holder's position if the tokenizer, custodian or any other intermediary fails; how corporate actions are applied to the token, and by whom; and who may convert the token into the share and back, and on what terms. The four rights the Order names run against the issuer, while the Commission's staff has identified a further exposure that none of them reaches, to the third party itself, "such as bankruptcy." Under the notice item on stoppage of trading, the venue should name which of three approaches to corporate actions under around-the-clock trading it uses (halting trading during corporate-action processing windows, treating the ledger as the authoritative record, or synchronizing two records), when an ex-date adjustment takes effect on the token, and how a dispute about it is resolved.
recommendations.refs: Section II.E; Notice items (h), (i) and (cc); Questions 1, 3 and 5

recommendations.ask: Extend the change-control disclosure from the venue's own contracts to every asset in its pools
recommendations.text: Extend the change-control disclosure from the venue's own contracts to every asset in its pools. Add a public-notice item listing, for each tokenized stock and each paired asset, every function by which any person can mint, burn, freeze, block, force the transfer of, pause, restrict the transfer of, or upgrade or replace the code governing the asset; the address at which it resides; who can exercise it; and whether its exercise requires approval by more than one person or is subject to a delay, revised within five business days of any change. Treat an exercise as a significant operational event under the Order when it freezes, blocks, burns or forces the transfer of units held by a pool the venue provides, or pauses transfers of an asset in that pool, or when the venue or a Covered Firm supplying the pool holds the function, and confirm that "auditable" in the Order's condition on a venue's smart contracts includes the authority to replace the audited code. The notice item on distributed ledger technology asks these questions only of the venue's own applications, and the program's verification of four major tokenized Treasury products, as documented in March 2026, found no timelock in any administrative control chain.
recommendations.refs: Section II.A; Notice items (h), (n) and (dd); Questions 1, 4 and 5; Section II.I

recommendations.ask: State, for each leg of a trade, when the transfer is final and who bears the loss if it is reversed or frozen
recommendations.text: State, for each leg of a trade, when the transfer is final and who bears the loss if it is reversed or frozen. Require the public notice's item on clearing and settlement to state, for each asset in a trading pair, the ledger event at which the venue treats the transfer as final; the legal effect of that event under the terms governing the asset, including whether it transfers the security or security entitlement or instructs an off-chain record; and how loss is allocated if a completed transfer is reversed by a reorganization of the ledger or the asset is frozen after execution. Settlement is "near instantaneous" only if the ledger event is the legal transfer for both assets. Every fiat-backed stablecoin in the MVEP's sample failed its settlement-finality category for want of a finality analysis comparable to the Uniform Commercial Code's funds-transfer article, and because a pool holds every liquidity provider's stablecoin at one contract address, a block on that address would freeze the stablecoin side of the whole pool.
recommendations.refs: Notice item (y); Questions 4, 5 and 7; UCC Article 4A

recommendations.ask: Add the ledger transaction identifier and the U.S. dollar conversion rate to each transaction record
recommendations.text: Add the ledger transaction identifier and the U.S. dollar conversion rate to each transaction record. Add to the minimum fields in the Order's transaction transparency condition the identifier of the transaction on the distributed ledger and, for any pair whose other asset is not denominated in U.S. dollars, the conversion rate used to state the price in dollars and the source of that rate; the venue already holds both when it computes the dollar price. Without the rate, a reader cannot tell a move in the stock from a move in the stablecoin it traded against: in the March 2023 banking stress one stablecoin fell 10.4 percent below par on an hourly decentralized-exchange volume-weighted basis and 13 percent at the centralized-exchange intraday low, so the choice of conversion source alone moved the measured price by more than two and a half percentage points. Without the identifier, no reported print can be reconciled to the ledger.

recommendations.ask: Ask Covered Firms for their control over the parameters of pools they supply and their share of each pool's liquidity
recommendations.text: Ask Covered Firms for their control over the parameters of pools they supply and their share of each pool's liquidity. Add to the Covered Firm notification, and to the records a Covered Firm must keep, any key, role or governance right held by the firm or its affiliates that can set or alter the parameters, fees, code or pause state of an automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pool it supplies, together with its share of each such pool's liquidity at the end of each calendar month. The Order names control over pricing as the conduct that may make liquidity provision dealing, and on a ledger that control is exercised through acts the Order itself lists. A supplier that trades against a pool's price does not set it; one that also holds the pool's parameter, fee or pause controls is in a different position, and the two facts distinguish one from the other.

recommendations.ask: Determine affiliation for the volume and symbol limits by who can exercise a pool's privileged functions
recommendations.text: Determine affiliation for the volume and symbol limits by who can exercise a pool's privileged functions. Confirm that control "by contract, or otherwise" in the Order's definition includes the ability to exercise the privileged functions described in Recommendation 2, so that, for the aggregation conditions, venues are affiliated where the same person, or persons acting together, can exercise those functions over an automated market maker (AMM) liquidity pool that each provides. On a ledger the decisive power over a pool can sit with a shared key holder across entities that are not affiliated in the corporate sense, as with the single multisignature wallet the program found controlling several tokenized Treasury products. The reading adds no new category of affiliation and no disclosure beyond Recommendation 2, and it does not reach a shared software vendor, data provider or node operator that holds no such function.

recommendations.ask: Address the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2028 offer-and-sale restriction before it applies to a venue's pairing of a payment stablecoin
recommendations.text: Address the GENIUS Act's July 18, 2028 offer-and-sale restriction before it applies to a venue's pairing of a payment stablecoin. With Treasury, state before July 18, 2028 how the GENIUS Act's offer-and-sale restriction applies to a venue's pairing of a payment stablecoin, and in the meantime require the Notice to identify, for each paired payment stablecoin, whether its issuer is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer. From that date, subject to exceptions, the Act makes it unlawful for a digital asset service provider to offer or sell a payment stablecoin to a person in the United States unless a permitted payment stablecoin issuer issued it. The date falls inside the Order's term, which runs to September 17, 2031, and a footnote to the Order leaves open whether a venue is a digital asset service provider. The comment does not ask the Commission to limit paired assets by type.

letters.title: FSB: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of AI
letters.headline: FSB AI Sound Practices response (first international standard-setter filing)
letters.h1: FSB AI Sound Practices response: composition-chain accountability, measured in live agentic payments
letters.description: Tokenization Systems' first international standard-setter response: the FSB consultation on Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of AI in finance.
letters.thesis: All seven consultation questions answered, anchored by the first control-layer measurement of live agentic payments: autonomous agents already executing irreversible payments through a settlement layer no institution governs.
letters.gaps: Contribution: two uncovered risk areas (cross-operator composition; integrity of AI-adoption statistics), a measured nonbank case study, three practice additions, and two glossary refinements.
letters.card_meta: 2026-07-01 · Financial Stability Board · MVEP-AI + CLII-AI · first international filing

recommendations.ask: Composition-chain documentation.
recommendations.text: Composition-chain documentation. For AI use cases with execution authority, document the full operator chain through settlement, including non-contractual settlement layers, and record who can halt, reverse, or remediate a transaction at each layer.

recommendations.ask: Execution-authority evidence package.
recommendations.text: Execution-authority evidence package. Name a minimum evidence package before any AI system receives authority to move funds or bind the institution, including a reconstructible authorization-context record, not merely a settlement record.

recommendations.ask: System-level dependency monitoring.
recommendations.text: System-level dependency monitoring. Acknowledge measured system-level concentration of shared AI-payment dependencies as a complement to institution-level registers, which cannot observe market-wide facilitator concentration.

recommendations.ask: Agentic-AI glossary distinction.
recommendations.text: Agentic-AI glossary distinction. Distinguish agentic AI generally from agentic AI with execution authority; advisory autonomy and irreversible transaction authority differ in kind.

recommendations.ask: Supply-chain scope.
recommendations.text: Supply-chain scope. Reconsider the service-relationship limit in "supply chain," or add "composition chain" as a companion term that reaches operators outside direct service relationships.

letters.title: SEC Transfer Agent Rules
letters.headline: SEC transfer agent rules comment
letters.h1: SEC transfer agent rules comment: when a security's ownership is recorded on a crypto network, say which record is the security and who controls it
letters.description: Letter to the SEC on its proposed transfer agent rules: say which record governs a tokenized security, reconcile on-chain supply to it, and define control on a shared ledger. Seven recommendations.
letters.thesis: The proposal lets a crypto network carry the master securityholder file, the authoritative record of who owns an issuer's securities, but does not say which record governs when a token and the off-chain file disagree, does not require that a token's supply be reconciled to the file, and does not define exclusive control for a ledger the transfer agent shares with everyone else on the network.
letters.gaps: Gaps: no rule says which record governs when a token and the off-chain file disagree; on-chain supply is never reconciled to the file, so tokens minted beyond it are neither a record difference nor an overissuance; exclusive control is undefined for a shared ledger, and viewing a public ledger counts as independent access; the rule text records the results of a token's privileged functions but never the functions or who holds them; the 15-day handover moves records but not keys; the annual report transfer agents file never links an issue to the network that carries its record.

recommendations.ask: State which record governs, reconcile on-chain supply to the master securityholder file every business day, and count excess supply in the overissuance test
recommendations.text: State which record governs, reconcile on-chain supply to the master securityholder file every business day, and count excess supply in the overissuance test. Require the recordkeeping transfer agent, for each tokenized issue, to designate in writing whether the crypto network is the master securityholder file, a component of it, or a copy, and which record governs if they disagree, and to disclose that designation to holders. Add to the rule's definition of a record difference the case where the quantity of a tokenized issue outstanding on any crypto network differs from the quantity the file records, reconciled at least every business day, so that a difference left unresolved is reported as an aged record difference. Count units outstanding on a network in excess of the file in the overissuance test, and extend the duty to resolve an overissuance to such supply, whoever created it. Decline the exemption the SEC's question floats for a file kept exclusively on an immutable blockchain network: a public ledger's history persists only while the network and its archive nodes do. As proposed, tokens minted beyond the file, by an exploit, a bridge to another network or an error, are neither a record difference nor an overissuance, although monitoring for overissuance is one of a transfer agent's statutory functions.

recommendations.ask: Define exclusive control of a ledger component as sole authority to create, cancel, or freeze units or move them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or exercised only on its instruction, under joint authorization
recommendations.text: Define exclusive control of a ledger component as sole authority to create, cancel, or freeze units or move them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or exercised only on its instruction, under joint authorization. The rule requires the transfer agent to keep "exclusive control" over the master securityholder file but does not define the term, and the release reads the ability to view a ledger and furnish copies as independent access; anyone can view and copy a public ledger. Define exclusive control, for any component of the file kept on a crypto network, as sole authority to create, cancel or freeze units, or to transfer them without the holder's authorization, held by the transfer agent or by a person acting only on its instruction under an agreement the transfer agent can terminate, and exercised under joint authorization of at least two persons it designates. Holders would still transfer their own units. The joint-authorization element follows the Commission's own custody proposal for advisers, and the standard parallels the control test the OCC adopted for custody under the GENIUS Act. Where a person other than the transfer agent can freeze or move units at the level of the network, as the Arbitrum Security Council did in emergency responses to two exploits in 2026, the transfer agent should identify that person to holders, and that network should carry only a copy of the record, with the off-chain file governing.

recommendations.ask: Treat the privileged functions of a token as transfer agent functions
recommendations.text: Treat the privileged functions of a token as transfer agent functions. The rule text records the results of a token's privileged functions, in the transfer journal's issuances, cancellations and transfers, but never names the functions or says who holds them. Require that each privileged function of a tokenized issue's own contract be held by the recordkeeping transfer agent or be exercisable only on its instruction; require issuer authorization for every creation or cancellation of units, as the transfer agent rules already require for changes to the control book; require joint authorization and a transfer journal entry for every use of a privileged function, including freezes, pauses and changes to the contract's logic, recording any instruction or legal order the use rests on; require disclosure to holders of which persons hold which functions; confirm that a resale restriction enforced in a token contract is a restrictive legend under the proposed rule on restrictive legends, so that lifting it is a removal subject to the rule; and name these functions in any guidance on what makes a risk material under the comprehensive risk management rule. These are transfer agent functions in fact; the rule should make them transfer agent functions in law.
recommendations.refs: Questions 50, 84, 109 and 140; rule 17ad-10(e); proposed rule 17ad-31; rule 17ad-12(a)(2)

recommendations.ask: Hand over control with the records, and plan for a transfer agent's failure
recommendations.text: Hand over control with the records, and plan for a transfer agent's failure. The proposal requires a departing transfer agent to deliver its records within fifteen calendar days. For a tokenized issue, records are not enough: a successor that receives the records but not the privileged roles of the token contract cannot correct, reissue or move units, and a withheld key gives a departing transfer agent the same leverage a withheld file does. Require the handover to include every privileged role and key the transfer agent holds or controls for each tokenized issue, or their revocation and reissue to the successor; require the business continuity plan the comprehensive risk management rule calls for to address network halts and forks, contract exploits, bridge failures, and loss or compromise of keys; and keep the rule that there can be only one recordkeeping transfer agent for an issue, applied across networks, so that one transfer agent is accountable for reconciling every representation of the issue. The release reports that of the 144 transfer agents that withdrew from registration between 2016 and 2025, 56 (39 percent) indicated a successor transfer agent for each issue; in a concentrated market, one transfer agent's failure can reach many tokenized issues at once.

recommendations.ask: Keep payment stablecoins and tokenized deposits out of "funds" unless held under stated conditions
recommendations.text: Keep payment stablecoins and tokenized deposits out of "funds" unless held under stated conditions. The SEC asks whether stablecoins and tokenized deposits can be the funds a transfer agent holds for issuers and securityholders. A token held for securityholders carries risks a deposit account does not: loss of keys, an issuer's freeze or redemption halt, and network failure. Permit them to stand in for funds only if they are payment stablecoins of permitted payment stablecoin issuers under the GENIUS Act, or deposit liabilities of a depository institution recorded on a crypto network; they are held by a bank or trust company in a for-the-benefit-of wallet, not by the transfer agent itself; the transfer agent keeps per-client records and reconciles them to the wallet's balance on the network at least every business day; and the business continuity plan addresses a freeze or redemption halt by the issuer. Segregate tokens the transfer agent holds for securityholders, such as undelivered distributions, from its own assets on the same terms the rule applies to funds.

recommendations.ask: Make tokenization visible in transfer agents' annual reports
recommendations.text: Make tokenization visible in transfer agents' annual reports. The report form's proposed new question counts the issues for which a registrant kept the master securityholder file using distributed ledger technology "in whole or in part," a count that lumps a ledger that is the whole official record with one that is only a component of it and misses a ledger that only copies it, and no question links an issue to the network that carries its record. Split that question into issues for which the ledger is the file, a component of it, or a synchronized copy; require, by issue and publicly, the network and contract address of each tokenized issue, as entries on the list of issues serviced that the amended form would already require; define the issuer-sponsored and third-party-sponsored models in the form instructions; and make the names of distributed ledger platforms and tokenization agents public. A contract address is already public on its network; the form would only connect it to the transfer agent of record, and asks for no key, wallet or holder information.
recommendations.refs: Questions 16, 19, 21 and 23; Form TA-2 Question 4(e); Form TA-2 Question 13

recommendations.ask: Make the wallet address part of position detail for tokenized positions, and address lost keys
recommendations.text: Make the wallet address part of position detail for tokenized positions, and address lost keys. Require the wallet address, and the network, as position detail for every tokenized position, in addition to, and not instead of, the holder's name and mailing address, with procedures for changes of address and for lost keys. A wallet address shows which key can move the units; it does not show who holds them, and it fails as a way to reach the holder at the moment that matters most, when the key is lost. In the rule on lost and inactive securityholders, define the transaction limb of account activity for tokenized positions as transactions initiated or directed by, and reasonably attributable to, the holder, and not an unsolicited incoming transfer or automatic distribution alone, since on many networks anyone can send a token to any address; and treat a holder as an unresponsive payee when a payment goes to a wallet that has shown no such transaction for the inactivity period, with the written notice sent to the mailing address of record, so that the holder can be found before its property is lost.

letters.title: FinCEN A7 Network Special Measure
letters.headline: FinCEN A7 Network special measure comment
letters.h1: FinCEN A7 Network comment: assign each crypto obligation to the party that can carry it out
letters.description: Letter to FinCEN on its proposed special measure against the A7 Network's Sub-Agents: supports the prohibition, and asks for listed addresses, a stated role for stablecoin issuers, and a safe harbor that separates blocking from returning. Five recommendations.
letters.thesis: The proposal places nearly all of its work on convertible virtual currency (CVC) on the receiving institution, although FinCEN itself assesses that there are "few, if any, readily available ways" for that institution to reject an incoming transfer before receipt, and it does not say what the rule would require of the payment stablecoin issuers that are about to become covered by it.
letters.gaps: Gaps: the proposed list identifies entities, while a blockchain transfer carries addresses, not names; payment stablecoin issuers become covered institutions by cross-reference, and neither proposal says what this rule then requires of them; the preamble's rule that OFAC blocking counts as compliance is not in the regulatory text; the safe harbor does not separate blocking from returning; the notice and records do not identify a transfer by its transaction hash.

recommendations.ask: Adopt the prohibition on transmittals of funds rather than special measures one through five
recommendations.text: Adopt the prohibition on transmittals of funds rather than special measures one through five. A7A5 transfers do not pass through correspondent accounts, and special measure five reaches only correspondent and payable-through accounts, a limit the President's Working Group on Digital Asset Markets identified in July 2025.

recommendations.ask: Deliver Sub-Agent addresses, not only names, and state the minimum screening expected for convertible virtual currency
recommendations.text: Deliver Sub-Agent addresses, not only names, and state the minimum screening expected for convertible virtual currency. A blockchain transfer carries addresses, not names. The list FinCEN shares through its FI-Portal should carry each Sub-Agent's known CVC addresses and blockchains and the A7A5 token contracts, including wrapped representations (separate tokens that stand for A7A5), in machine-readable form. The prohibition should reach a transmittal sent from or to a listed address; funds that passed through a listed address at some earlier point, and arrived from an address that is not on the list, should be handled through risk-based due diligence and suspicious activity reporting.

recommendations.ask: State what the prohibition requires of payment stablecoin issuers, which become covered financial institutions by cross-reference
recommendations.text: State what the prohibition requires of payment stablecoin issuers, which become covered financial institutions by cross-reference. When FinCEN's pending issuer rule is final, permitted payment stablecoin issuers will become covered institutions under this rule automatically. Prohibit their primary market dealings with listed Sub-Agents (issuing, redeeming, converting, or holding stablecoins for them), require, or at least recognize as compliance, a prompt freeze of a listed address that holds their stablecoin, and state that the rule does not require blanket monitoring of secondary market transfers (transfers between other holders).

recommendations.ask: Put in the regulatory text the preamble's rule that OFAC blocking counts as compliance, and separate blocking from returning in the CVC safe harbor
recommendations.text: Put in the regulatory text the preamble's rule that OFAC blocking counts as compliance, and separate blocking from returning in the CVC safe harbor. In the provision that protects an institution after it receives CVC from a Sub-Agent, state separately when to block and when to reject and return, and say what to do when return is not feasible.

recommendations.ask: Identify CVC transfers by transaction hash in the notice and records, and treat returns and freezes as permitted disclosures
recommendations.text: Identify CVC transfers by transaction hash in the notice and records, and treat returns and freezes as permitted disclosures. For CVC, identify each transfer by its transaction hash, its unique public identifier, in the required notice and records, and confirm that a return transfer or an issuer freeze, both visible on the public blockchain, is a permitted disclosure even though FinCEN's list is non-public.
